subject: Request: EU-only debug trace snapshot for Artemis Therapeutics (timebound exception)
messages:
From: Lydia Park <lydia.park@artemis-thera.com>
To: jonas.weber@redwood-inference.com
Cc: security@artemis-thera.com
Date: Tue, 12 Sep 2028 16:14:00 +0100
Subject: Short-term EU trace export request for incident ART-7221

Hi Jonas,

We're troubleshooting a failure in our integration with Redwood that reproduced only for EU-hosted tenants. Our engineers need a timeboxed export of request/response traces tied to tenant/artemis-thera (no user account data required) to reproduce the issue locally. We understand retention policies — this will be a strictly temporary access request.

Request details:
- Scope: traces for tenant "artemis-thera" only, EU region (no cross-region exports)
- Time window: 2028-09-10 22:00 to 2028-09-11 03:00 CEST
- Purpose: reproduce intermittent auth timeouts in our end-to-end tests
- Access model requested: secure, download link accessible to Artemis security for 72 hours, then automated deletion

Can Redwood provide this as a timebound exception? If required, we can sign an exception document and accept a redaction step if there are PII concerns.

Appreciate a quick runbook for next steps — we've got a demo with our QA team on Friday.

Thanks,
Lydia Park
Platform Engineering
Artemis Therapeutics


From: jonas.weber@redwood-inference.com
To: marissa.cole@redwood-inference.com, lauren.bishop@redwood-inference.com
Cc: evelyn.hart@redwood-inference.com
Date: Tue, 12 Sep 2028 09:38:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Short-term EU trace export request for incident ART-7221

Marissa / Lauren — forwarding Artemis' request. They want a 72-hour downloadable export for a specific EU tenant time window. They offer to sign an exception doc and are open to redaction.

Questions:
- Is 72 hours acceptable from a policy/legal standpoint?
- Can SRE produce an EU-only archive and apply a PII redaction filter before we hand it over?
- What audit controls / approvals do we need in place (DocuSign + internal runbook sign-off?)

Context: Artemis is a mid-market customer on Dedicated EU capacity; this bug is blocking an internal QA gating step and they requested an expedited path. I can own comms if we get greenlight.

Next step ask: please advise recommended TTL, any guardrails we must enforce, and whether we need to route to ComplianceOps for an exception ticket.

— Jonas
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: marissa.cole@redwood-inference.com
To: jonas.weber@redwood-inference.com, lauren.bishop@redwood-inference.com
Cc: evelyn.hart@redwood-inference.com
Date: Tue, 12 Sep 2028 10:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Short-term EU trace export request for incident ART-7221

Thanks for the ping. Quick take from Security/Compliance: we can support a timebound export but only under these conditions — we should push these requirements back to Artemis in our reply.

Required controls:
- TTL: limit access to 48 hours rather than 72 (shorter windows reduce risk).
- Scope enforcement: SRE must produce a tarball that contains only service traces/headers (no full payloads). If payloads are essential, they must be redacted according to our PII tokenization runbook.
- EU residency: export and any temporary storage must remain in the EU (customer asked for this already). Archive must be stored in an EU-only S3 bucket with server-side encryption and KMS keys scoped to eu-1.
- Audit: generate an access audit record listing who downloaded the archive; we require Artemis to provide the list of recipients for the download link beforehand.
- Legal: signed timebound exception (DocuSign) acknowledging limited use and confirming deletion obligations.

I've attached our standard exception form and a minimal manifest sample that SRE can use to validate the archive contents.

SRE/Evelyn — can you confirm the feasibility of: extracting traces for the exact tenant/time window, running the PII redaction filter, and producing an encrypted archive with a 48h presigned download link in eu-1? Also confirm the steps to auto-delete and the audit events we will emit.

Marissa Cole
Senior Security Program Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachments: artemis_debug_request_20280912.pdf; trace_manifest_snippet.json
From: evelyn.hart@redwood-inference.com
To: marissa.cole@redwood-inference.com, jonas.weber@redwood-inference.com
Cc: lauren.bishop@redwood-inference.com
Date: Wed, 13 Sep 2028 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Short-term EU trace export request for incident ART-7221

Thanks — SRE can do this with the following constraints and steps. High-level plan below; fine-grained runbook will be created in Confluence and linked in the DocuSign envelope.

Feasibility and constraints:
- We can extract the tenant-scoped traces for the requested time window from EU-only shards.
- By default, traces include request/response payloads. Redaction step will strip user-level identifiers (emails, phone numbers, full-text user messages) using our tokenization pipeline. We'll keep minimal headers (request id, timestamp, route) and truncated response status/body snippets (first 120 chars) unless Artemis insists on full payloads.
- We will produce an encrypted tar.gz, upload to eu-1 S3, generate a presigned URL that expires in 48h, and enable access logging on the object.
- Auto-deletion: a lifecycle job will delete the object after 7 days from upload if not downloaded — but we can schedule a deletion task to remove the object immediately after the 48h presigned window closes.

Action items and ETA:
- Legal/Compliance: sign exception template (DocuSign).
- Artemis: return the list of intended recipients for the download link and sign the DocuSign.
- SRE: start extraction once we have the signed envelope; estimate 12 hours to produce archive and run redaction for a single 5-hour window.

If Legal insists on 72 hours rather than 48, we can escalate but Security prefers 48.

Evelyn Hart
Sr. SRE Manager, Redwood Inference

From: lauren.bishop@redwood-inference.com
To: jonas.weber@redwood-inference.com, evelyn.hart@redwood-inference.com
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood-inference.com
Date: Fri, 15 Sep 2028 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Short-term EU trace export request for incident ART-7221

I've reviewed and approve the request on the condition that Artemis signs the exception we attach and confirms the recipient list. Approved parameters: 48h access, EU-only storage, PII redaction as proposed, and mandatory audit logging.

Please proceed with this workflow:
1) Jonas: reply to Artemis outlining the controls and attach the DocuSign link (I've pre-approved the envelope text). Ask them to sign and return the recipient list.
2) Artemis signs DocuSign within 24 hours.
3) Evelyn/SRE: upon signed envelope, run the extraction and redaction; provide ETA and the presigned URL to Jonas.
4) Marissa/Security: confirm audit logging is enabled and retain the access log snapshot as part of the exception ticket.

Jonas — please include the following in your reply to Artemis (copy below): the 48h window we propose (we'll push back on 72), the requirement to sign, and the filename pattern we will use so they can whitelist the download: redwood-artemis-traces-20280910T22_20280911T03.tar.gz.enc

I'll mark the exception as approved in the ComplianceOps tracker once we receive the signed DocuSign.

Thanks,
Lauren Bishop
Head of Legal — Redwood Inference
